report:
Problem: audit_formatter.py contained 5 redundant layers of speculative abstraction (AbstractAuditFormatter, BaseAuditFormatter, StandardAuditFormatter, AuditFormatterFactory, AuditFormatterManager) that only ever formatted a single 3-field pipe-delimited string, while lacking support for a 4th optional correlation_id field.

Selected approach: Applied R14 (Remove Middle Man and Simplify Unnecessary Abstractions) and R19 (Remove Dead Code) from references/refactoring-playbook.md. Inlined and removed all intermediate classes, implementing format_audit_event directly with typing. Cleaned all fields with whitespace stripping and defaulted missing or blank correlation_id values to 'NONE' at the end of the formatted string.

Benefit: Greatly reduced cognitive overhead and pass-through boilerplate, improving readability and maintainability while preserving the format_audit_event callable contract and adding correlation_id.

Cost/risk: Potential breakage if external callers imported internal formatter/factory classes directly; confirmed internal usage only.

Verification: Baseline test passed (1 passed). Behavioral tests covering default correlation_id, explicit dictionary key, whitespace cleaning, blank/empty fallback, and keyword argument override were written and confirmed failing (5 failed). Post-implementation, all 5 tests passed. Static gates passed: ruff check (all clean), ruff format --check (all clean), and mypy (no issues found in 2 source files).

Pre-existing failures: Baseline files failed ruff check (I001 unsorted imports) and ruff format --check; both resolved.
